title: Original pad to a USB or Bluetooth keyboard, pad-ble v1
intro: One original NES controller into an ESP32, presented to a phone or a laptop as a plain keyboard: the bridge's own pad poll with a host interface behind it. No Pi, no UNO, no console. Sheets 2 to 4 are the C6 design, kept as a record; that board died 2026-09-29.

TWO BUILDS, ONE CIRCUIT. USB on a Waveshare ESP32-P4-Module-DEV-KIT (sheets 5 to 10), proven 2026-09-27. BLE on a classic ESP32-WROOM-32 devkit (sheets 11 to 15, 2026-09-30) on D25, D26, D27, since GPIO6 is its flash and GPIO3 its console; it advertises and the bench head bonded with it. No pad wired to it yet; no phone tried on either.
revisions: drawn as the buildable subset of the pad adapter: no cell, no charger, no switch
S3 pin numbers removed; GPIO4, GPIO5 and GPIO15 are strapping pins on the C6
one pullup per pad: R1 and R2 had both been drawn on pad 1's data line
A
devkit headers read off the part, breadboard sheet drawn from them
B
the second pad removed: a keyboard report has six key slots, and it was never sent
C
the sheet's own summary stopped saying a second pad is polled; it is not
D
the devkit's two header rows were drawn swapped; every address moves from row J to row A
E
the board built is the Waveshare ESP32-P4-Module-DEV-KIT; its header read from the vendor schematic and added as a sheet
F
the P4 gets its own three drawings; three of the five lead colours in rev E were typed, not read, and are corrected
G
GPIO37 and GPIO38 move from free to spoken for: they are the console UART, and nothing on the board claims them
H
the five holes are a contiguous run around the second 3V3, skipping 0; the ESP side measured and correct
I
the build is USB, not BLE: the hosted link to the module's C6 crashes BLE init, and the P4 has real USB OTG
J
the first pad was a replica; an original's lead colours differ, and red and yellow are different signals on each
K
J1 drawn as an original pad in its own colours on all three P4 sheets; rev J only captioned the replica's
L
measure-first item 4 closed and the host result on the cover and sheet 5; the DEVICE jumper note removed, it belongs to the high-speed switch
M
the BLE build moves to a classic ESP32-WROOM-32 devkit, the C6 being dead: three sheets and a header page of its own, pins D25, D26, D27 read off the board
